text:
Advantage Investment Management LLC Sells 1,296 Shares of Apple (AAPL) Posted by Paula Ricardo | Apr 4th, 2018 
Advantage Investment Management LLC cut its stake in shares of Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 3.4% in the 3rd quarter, according to the company in its most recent filing with the Securities & Exchange Commission. The fund owned 36,718 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after selling 1,296 shares during the period. Apple makes up 1.8% of Advantage Investment Management LLC’s investment portfolio, making the stock its 13th biggest holding. Advantage Investment Management LLC’s holdings in Apple were worth $5,659,000 as of its most recent filing with the Securities & Exchange Commission. 
A number of other hedge funds and other institutional investors have also added to or reduced their stakes in AAPL. Nomura Asset Management Co. Ltd. raised its position in shares of Apple by 17.6% in the 3rd quarter. Nomura Asset Management Co. Ltd. now owns 1,456,882 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $224,534,000 after buying an additional 217,640 shares during the period. Lido Advisors LLC increased its holdings in Apple by 23.2% in the 3rd quarter. Lido Advisors LLC now owns 65,796 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $11,122,000 after purchasing an additional 12,395 shares in the last quarter. B. Riley Financial Inc. increased its holdings in Apple by 49.6% in the 3rd quarter. B. Riley Financial Inc. now owns 15,951 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $2,458,000 after purchasing an additional 5,290 shares in the last quarter. Caisse DE Depot ET Placement DU Quebec increased its holdings in Apple by 1.3% in the 3rd quarter. Caisse DE Depot ET Placement DU Quebec now owns 2,460,494 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $380,807,000 after purchasing an additional 32,500 shares in the last quarter. Finally, Clear Perspective Advisors LLC increased its holdings in Apple by 5.2% in the 3rd quarter. Clear Perspective Advisors LLC now owns 16,817 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $2,592,000 after purchasing an additional 827 shares in the last quarter. Institutional investors own 61.35% of the company’s stock. Get Apple alerts: 
In other news, insider Daniel J. Riccio sold 15,641 shares of the business’s stock in a transaction dated Friday, January 5th. The shares were sold at an average price of $174.78, for a total transaction of $2,733,733.98. Following the transaction, the insider now owns 13,739 shares in the company, valued at approximately $2,401,302.42. The transaction was disclosed in a legal filing with the SEC, which is accessible through the SEC website . Insiders own 0.06% of the company’s stock. 
Apple stock traded up $3.22 on Wednesday, reaching $171.61. 34,597,344 shares of the stock were exchanged, compared to its average volume of 37,558,172. The firm has a market cap of $845,736.50, a price-to-earnings ratio of 18.63, a P/E/G ratio of 1.26 and a beta of 1.25. The company has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.74, a current ratio of 1.24 and a quick ratio of 1.20. Apple has a twelve month low of $140.06 and a twelve month high of $183.50. 
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last released its earnings results on Thursday, February 1st. The iPhone maker reported $3.89 earnings per share for the quarter, topping the Zacks’ consensus estimate of $3.82 by $0.07. Apple had a net margin of 21.13% and a return on equity of 37.37%. The firm had revenue of $88.29 billion during the quarter, compared to analyst estimates of $87.62 billion. During the same quarter in the previous year, the business earned $3.36 EPS. The business’s revenue was up 12.7% on a year-over-year basis. sell-side analysts expect that Apple will post 11.37 earnings per share for the current year. 
AAPL has been the subject of several recent research reports. UBS set a $190.00 price target on Apple and gave the company a “buy” rating in a report on Friday, January 5th. Morgan Stanley restated a “buy” rating and set a $205.00 target price (up from $200.00) on shares of Apple in a research note on Tuesday, January 23rd. Sanford C. Bernstein downgraded Apple from an “outperform” rating to a “market perform” rating and lowered their target price for the company from $195.00 to $170.00 in a research note on Friday, February 2nd. HSBC set a $204.00 target price on Apple and gave the company a “buy” rating in a research note on Tuesday, January 30th. Finally, Vetr upgraded Apple from a “hold” rating to a “buy” rating and set a $184.49 price target for the company in a research note on Monday, March 5th. One research analyst has rated the stock with a sell rating, eighteen have assigned a hold rating, thirty-one have issued a buy rating and one has issued a strong buy rating to the company’s stock. Apple has a consensus rating of “Buy” and a consensus price target of $202.52.
